manifest.pairing: Two climbs are paired when their summits are within 400 m of each other and they belong to different races — matched by where they are, not by what they are called, because 424 of these climbs have no published name. A pair means the two end in the same place. It does not mean they are the same ascent: approach direction is not compared, and a col climbed from opposite sides pairs here. The measured separation travels with every pair so a 12 m match and a 380 m match are not read as the same claim.
manifest.method: Climbs are detected from this project's own elevation series by tools/derive/build_profiles.py, not read from any published climb list. Where the organiser categorised a climb whose summit falls within the matching window, its name and category are carried alongside — never merged into — the detected figures.
manifest.difficulty_model: fiets/1.0 — the index published by the Dutch magazine Fiets: H²/(D×10) + (T−1000)/1000 for summits above 1000 m, with H the height gain in metres, D the length in metres and T the summit altitude. Both terms are emitted separately. The formula is somebody else's; the numbers put into it are this project's own measurements, and differ from published Fiets figures wherever the detected extent of a climb differs from the conventional one.
manifest.limitations: A detected climb is an extent found on one route version, and its foot is where the detector's rules put it rather than where a road sign does. Ascent is the sum of positive elevation change along the detected span, so it exceeds the summit-minus-foot difference wherever the road undulates. max_grad is a single sample pair and carries the elevation series' full noise; steepest_km averages over roughly a kilometre and is the figure to compare climbs by.
